sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3. Languoid page Papavô (papa1263), family 'Unattested'. Accessed 2026-09-17.
sources.note: Nothing. Page states 'Retired in ISO 639-3: Any usage probably referred to one of: Amarakaeri [amr], Huachipaeri [hug], Kulina [cul], Amahuaca [amc], or Yawanawa [ywn]'; reason non-existent; 0 descriptive references (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology; the three refs attached are all listed by Glottolog as an overview ethnological works).
Nothing; one line: 'Papavô [ppv] – name given to several uncontacted groups'.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2008. Change Request Number 2008-019: retire [ppv] Papavô (submitted by David Holbrook, SIL; adopted 2009-01-16). 5 pp.
sources.note: Nothing about stress or any linguistic feature. p.2 section 3(c): 'This is a name that was used to refer to a group of several different uncontacted groups.. there are four separate, now identified groups that fell under this label.. Harakmbet--two languages, Amarakaeri [amr] and Huachipaeri [hug]; Kulina [cul]; Amahuaca [amc]; and Yawanawa [ywn]'. Reason for retirement: 'There is no evidence that the language exists.' Only cited source is Bahuchet (ed.), The situation of indigenous peoples in tropical forests, Report 34 (dead lucy.ukc.ac.uk link).
